findings.body:
**Reviewer note:** this review was produced by Claude (Fable 5.2), not a GPT-tier model, so it does not supply the cross-family independence the prompt assumes. I worked only from the inlined text.

## Verdict: MINOR ISSUES

**1. DESIGN — Tier-1 reports have no guaranteed reader outside Echo (§Every development tier; §Multi-machine posture).**
The spec says the advisory runs on every trace, on every machine. The only named reader for a Tier-1 change that skips build is Echo's bugs-overseer on one Mac Studio, and only for bugs it tracks. Any other Tier-1 commit, on any other agent, produces a warning nobody is assigned to read. With no veto, that is the Tier-1 gap again, now with a report attached.
*Resolution:* name the fleet-wide reader for that path, or state plainly that coverage there is print-to-builder only.

**2. DESIGN — The independent reviewer is handed the advisory report before judging (§Every development tier).**
The spec's own problem statement objects to an unreviewed prescription anchoring the builder. Rule 27 says a dispatch withholds the expected answer. Yet every reviewer receives the pair and the report together.
*Resolution:* the reviewer records its own constitutional assessment first, then reconciles against the report; test that ordering.

**3. DESIGN (borderline) — No measure of whether the advisory works (§Tests; §Maturation; Rule 39).**
This is the likeliest failure mode: the advisory is persistently unavailable, or its findings are ignored. A prompt near 256 KiB under one 180-second request with no retry may time out routinely. Outcome classes are audited but nothing aggregates them.
*Resolution:* have the overseer's existing ledger report the unavailable rate and the findings-engaged rate; no new job needed.

**4. PRECISION — Coverage shrinks as changes grow (§Automated executor).**
The spec's own example (192-KiB diff plus 94-KiB pair) shows the largest fixes get safety-only review. I did not measure the 94 KiB figure; it looks plausible from the inlined text. The fallback is honest, but say outright that constitutional coverage is weakest on the largest changes.

**5. PRECISION — Freshness check is a byte comparison owned by an LLM-driven job (§Governing context).**
The spec notes Rule 119's daily pairing check is not scheduled, then routes around it. Running the comparison at release time would be simpler and would not depend on Echo. The stated objection to a submodule ("pins stale bytes") applies equally to vendoring; the real reason is the runtime checkout.

**6. PRECISION — Secret-detector match means no review at all.**
Fixes that touch detector fixtures or fake credentials will be permanently unreviewable. Note the expected fallback.

**7. PRECISION — Undefined local terms.**
"ELI16", "tier", "trace", "fix and design heads", "pool job" and "ladder: feedbackFactory.execute" are never defined. Also "explicitly cover" should be "covers".

**Checked and consistent with the inlined rules:**
- The Foundation-limits claims about Rules 49 and 118 match the rule text.
- The purpose's draft status and the Rule/Value distinction are preserved.
- No keyword blocker is added (Rules 10, 12, 86).
- The simplestRobustRoute, multi-machine and team posture fields are present.

**Not verifiable from the inlined context:**
- That the conformance check's opening names the 2.0 pair as governing.
- The `crossModelReviewer.ts:107–152` derivation of the transport allowance.
- The 180-second deadline.
